then.say: Mind the smoke, it follows the pretty ones. Ulla. That lump by the fire is my Jost.
We walked from the coast to see the Wick burn. Three months on foot. It was smaller than they said.

do.say: Jost's knees won't take the road home. And the Order don't open the Abbey gate for pilgrims any more.
So we wait. Everyone at Wick's Rest is waiting for something. Keeps the fire fed.
Pilgrims who came up the road and didn't go back down it. Agnes tends them. She knew most of them.
Every stone's got a candle. The candles in the Drip burn crooked, so they all lean toward the Abbey.

then.say: The fire's catching better since the bell went quiet. Don't ask me why. I'm just glad.

else.say: Come and sit when you're tired. There's always a spot on the log.
